sector_model: Florida Panhandle land developer, hospitality and leasing operator: real estate sales timing, JV land sales, hotel EBITDA, book value, debt; operating cash flow before development spending; nonfinancial FCF incomplete
thesis: The St. Joe Company trades at 69.97 (2026-11-06 close), market cap about 3.96B on 56,524,851 shares (cover, 2026-10-26): about 33x TTM diluted EPS of about 2.11 and about 5.2x stockholders' equity of 765.1M. TTM revenue 542.9M, net income 121.3M and operating cash flow 188.3M (FY2025 10-K plus nine-month deltas). Nine months 2026: revenue +7.7% to 414.1M, net income +6.6% to 91.3M, EPS 1.60 vs 1.48. Debt net 361.7M plus 179.1M senior notes held by a special purpose entity against 117.9M cash; buybacks 65.4M in 9M2026 (vs 25.1M) and dividends 0.16 a quarter.
counterthesis: The multiple already prices sustained development, and the quarter was weaker underneath: Q3 revenue fell 3.0% and net income 4.6%, real estate revenue included 31.4M of net present value from land sold to the Latitude Margaritaville Watersound joint venture (10.9M of intra-entity profit eliminated and deferred), equity income from JVs swung to a 8.2M loss in Q3 (218K loss in 9M vs 21.2M income), and leasing revenue is shrinking (-11.4% in 9M). Real estate earnings are lumpy and depend on Florida demand, hurricanes, insurance cost and rates. Capital spending on real estate development is not isolated here (XBRL PP&E purchases are only 3.8M a year), so cash flow overstates distributable earnings. Equity of 765M and a 5.2x price to book leave little cushion.
invalidation: Quarterly real estate sales and homesite pricing falling for two or more quarters; hospitality revenue growth turning negative; JV losses continuing; operating cash flow after development investment turning negative; buybacks funded by debt.
